title: VLOOKUP pulls the wrong column after someone inserts one

payoff.headline:
VLOOKUP COUNTS
COLUMNS
payoff.sub: Insert one column and column two is suddenly a different column. XLOOKUP points at the one you meant.

script.vo: Your lookup came back with a department code this morning. Nobody touched the formula.
Account codes on the left, amounts beside them.

the amounts.

script.caption:

For months.

script.caption:
Somebody inserts

script.vo: Column two used to be the amount. Column two is the department now.

script.vo: VLOOKUP counts columns. It has no idea which one you meant.
script.caption:
It counts. It doesn't
know what you meant.

script.vo: So point at the column instead. XLOOKUP takes the account column and the amount column.
script.caption:

script.vo: Any formula that counts columns is one insert away from quietly lying to you.

post.title: VLOOKUP returns the wrong column after inserting a column
post.description:
vlookup returns wrong value after inserting a column in excel
VLOOKUP's column number is a count, not a reference, so an inserted column silently shifts what column two means. XLOOKUP points at the actual column and survives the insert.
